Agrarian_Party_of_Ukraine.name: Agrarian Party of Ukraine
Agrarian_Party_of_Ukraine.summary: Farmers' party, refounded in 2006, that entered several central and northern oblast councils in 2015.

All-Ukrainian_Union_\"Cherkashchany\".name: All-Ukrainian Union "Cherkashchany"
All-Ukrainian_Union_\"Cherkashchany\".summary: Regional party of Cherkasy Oblast, associated with the businessman and MP Volodymyr Zubyk; second in the oblast council in 2015 and first in 2020.

Batkivshchyna.name: Batkivshchyna (Fatherland)
Batkivshchyna.summary: Yulia Tymoshenko's party, founded in 1999; consistently among the larger factions in central Ukraine's councils from 2006 to 2020.

Bolsheviks.name: Bolsheviks
Bolsheviks.summary: Lenin's faction of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party, which seized power in Petrograd in November 1917 and fought the Ukrainian People's Republic for control of Ukraine.

Borotbists.name: Borotbists
Borotbists.summary: Left wing of the Ukrainian SRs that allied with the Bolsheviks in 1919 and merged into the Communist Party (Bolsheviks) of Ukraine in 1920, many members later leading Ukrainization.

Communist_Party_of_Ukraine.name: Communist Party of Ukraine
Communist_Party_of_Ukraine.summary: Successor party refounded in 1993 that was the largest party in the Verkhovna Rada in the 1990s and strong in rural central and eastern Ukraine; banned by court order in 2015 under decommunization laws.

Communist_Party_of_Ukraine_(Soviet_Union.name: Communist Party of Ukraine (Soviet Union)
Communist_Party_of_Ukraine_(Soviet_Union.summary: The Ukrainian branch of the Soviet Communist Party and the sole ruling party of the Ukrainian SSR from 1919-1920 until it was banned in August 1991.

Constitutional_Democratic_Party.name: Constitutional Democratic Party
Constitutional_Democratic_Party.leaning: Centre to centre-right, liberalism, constitutional monarchism
Constitutional_Democratic_Party.summary: Russian liberal party of the professional middle classes; in Ukraine it drew support mainly in towns and opposed Ukrainian territorial autonomy.

European_Solidarity.name: European Solidarity (Petro Poroshenko Bloc 'Solidarity')
European_Solidarity.summary: Petro Poroshenko's party, which as 'Solidarity' won the most seats in almost every central oblast council in 2015 and was renamed European Solidarity in 2019.

For_the_Future_(political_party).name: For the Future (Za maibutnie)
For_the_Future_(political_party).summary: Party built around MP Ihor Palytsia and linked to Ihor Kolomoyskyi, which won seats in every central oblast council in 2020.

Holos_(Ukraine).name: Holos (Voice)
Holos_(Ukraine).summary: Liberal party founded by the rock singer Sviatoslav Vakarchuk in 2019, with its strongest local result in Kyiv in 2020.

Leonid_Chernovetskyi_Bloc.name: Leonid Chernovetskyi Bloc
Leonid_Chernovetskyi_Bloc.summary: Electoral bloc of the banker Leonid Chernovetskyi, who won the Kyiv mayoralty in 2006 and 2008; his bloc led the Kyiv City Council until the 2014 elections.

Mensheviks.name: Mensheviks
Mensheviks.summary: The moderate faction of Russian social democracy, influential in urban soviets in 1917 but marginal in the Constituent Assembly vote in Ukraine.

Native_Home.name: Native Home (Ridnyi dim)
Native_Home.summary: Party associated with Chernihiv mayor Vladyslav Atroshenko, which came first in the Chernihiv Oblast Council election in 2020.

Nazi_Party.name: Nazi Party
Nazi_Party.summary: Germany's ruling party, whose officials ran the civil administration of the Reichskommissariat Ukraine in 1941-1944 under Erich Koch, with mass murder of Jews and forced labour deportations.

Opposition_Bloc.name: Opposition Bloc
Opposition_Bloc.summary: Successor alliance to the Party of Regions formed in 2014, with a presence in some central oblast councils in 2015.

Opposition_Platform_–_For_Life.name: Opposition Platform — For Life
Opposition_Platform_–_For_Life.summary: Main pro-Russian opposition party after 2018, led by Yuriy Boyko and Viktor Medvedchuk; suspended in March 2022 and banned by court in June 2022.

Our_Land_(Ukraine).name: Our Land (Nash Krai)
Our_Land_(Ukraine).summary: Party founded in 2011 that drew many former Party of Regions local officials and did well in local elections in 2015 and 2020.

Our_Ukraine_(political_party).name: Our Ukraine
Our_Ukraine_(political_party).summary: Party and electoral bloc of Viktor Yushchenko; its governors ran the oblasts after the 2004 Orange Revolution, but its support collapsed by 2010.

Party_of_Regions.name: Party of Regions
Party_of_Regions.summary: Party of Viktor Yanukovych based in the Donbas; after his 2010 election its appointees governed every oblast until the 2014 Revolution of Dignity, after which it collapsed.

Party_of_Veterans_of_Afghanistan.name: Party of Veterans of Afghanistan
Party_of_Veterans_of_Afghanistan.summary: Small party representing veterans of the Soviet-Afghan War, which won seats in the Cherkasy Oblast Council in 2015.

People's_Democratic_Party_(Ukraine).name: People's Democratic Party
People's_Democratic_Party_(Ukraine).summary: Pro-presidential 'party of power' of the late 1990s, associated with Prime Minister Valeriy Pustovoitenko and with many regional officials appointed under President Kuchma.

People's_Party_(Ukraine).name: People's Party
People's_Party_(Ukraine).summary: Party of former Verkhovna Rada chairman Volodymyr Lytvyn, with a regional base in Zhytomyr Oblast, where Lytvyn comes from.

Proposition_(political_party).name: Proposition
Proposition_(political_party).summary: 'Party of Mayors' founded in 2020 by six city mayors, including those of Zhytomyr and Kropyvnytskyi.

Radical_Party_of_Oleh_Liashko.name: Radical Party of Oleh Liashko
Radical_Party_of_Oleh_Liashko.summary: Populist party of Oleh Liashko with a rural base, notably strong in Chernihiv Oblast, Liashko's home region.

Revival_(Ukraine).name: Revival (Vidrodzhennia)
Revival_(Ukraine).summary: Party formed largely by former Party of Regions politicians, linked to the oligarch Ihor Kolomoyskyi, which entered several councils in 2015.

Self_Reliance_(political_party).name: Self Reliance (Samopomich)
Self_Reliance_(political_party).summary: Party of Lviv mayor Andriy Sadovyi that did well in 2014-2015, including second place in Kyiv in 2015, but fell out of most councils in 2020.

Servant_of_the_People.name: Servant of the People
Servant_of_the_People.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky's party, which won a parliamentary majority in 2019; in the 2020 local elections it often came first or second but rarely won outright.

Socialist_Party_of_Ukraine.name: Socialist Party of Ukraine
Socialist_Party_of_Ukraine.summary: Party of Oleksandr Moroz founded in 1991, with its strongest base in rural central Ukraine (Poltava, Vinnytsia, Kirovohrad, Cherkasy); it backed the Orange Revolution but declined after 2006. Banned in 2022.

Socialist_Revolutionary_Party.name: Socialist Revolutionary Party
Socialist_Revolutionary_Party.summary: The main all-Russian peasant socialist party, which won the 1917 Constituent Assembly election nationwide; in Ukraine it often ran joint lists with the Ukrainian SRs.

Strength_and_Honor.name: Strength and Honor
Strength_and_Honor.summary: Party led by former security service chief Ihor Smeshko, which won council seats in Zhytomyr Oblast in 2020.

Svoboda_(Ukraine).name: Svoboda (All-Ukrainian Union 'Freedom')
Svoboda_(Ukraine).summary: Nationalist party led by Oleh Tiahnybok, strongest in Galicia but represented in Kyiv and several central councils in 2014-2015.

Ukrainian_Democratic_Alliance_for_Reform.name: UDAR (Ukrainian Democratic Alliance for Reform)
Ukrainian_Democratic_Alliance_for_Reform.summary: Vitali Klitschko's party, founded in 2010; it won the Kyiv City Council in 2014, merged into the Petro Poroshenko Bloc in 2015 and ran separately again in 2020, keeping Klitschko as mayor.

Ukrainian_Social_Democratic_Labour_Party.name: Ukrainian Social Democratic Labour Party
Ukrainian_Social_Democratic_Labour_Party.summary: Marxist Ukrainian party of Volodymyr Vynnychenko and Symon Petliura that led the General Secretariat of the Central Rada and later the Directorate.

Ukrainian_Socialist-Revolutionary_Party.name: Ukrainian Socialist-Revolutionary Party
Ukrainian_Socialist-Revolutionary_Party.summary: Peasant-based socialist party formed in 1917 that was the largest faction in the Central Rada and won the 1917 Constituent Assembly vote across most Ukrainian governorates; it split in 1918, its left wing becoming the Borotbists.

Ukrainian_Strategy_of_Groysman.name: Ukrainian Strategy of Groysman
Ukrainian_Strategy_of_Groysman.summary: Party of former Prime Minister and Vinnytsia mayor Volodymyr Groysman, dominant in Vinnytsia Oblast and city since 2020.

UKROP.name: UKROP (Ukrainian Association of Patriots)
UKROP.summary: Nationalist party linked to Ihor Kolomoyskyi and veterans of the Donbas war, which entered many oblast councils in 2015 and later merged into For the Future.

Unity_of_Oleksandr_Omelchenko.name: Unity of Oleksandr Omelchenko
Unity_of_Oleksandr_Omelchenko.summary: Kyiv-based party of Oleksandr Omelchenko, mayor of Kyiv from 1996 to 2006, which remained a mid-sized faction on the city council.

x:Native_City_(Ridne_Misto).name: Native City (Ridne Misto)
x:Native_City_(Ridne_Misto).summary: Poltava-based local party, represented in the Poltava Oblast Council in 2015 and 2020. No English Wikipedia article; source: Poltava Oblast Council article, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poltava_Oblast_Council.

x:People's_Will_(Sumy).name: People's Will
x:People's_Will_(Sumy).summary: Party listed with six seats in the Sumy Oblast Council after the 2015 election; its exact identity is not described on English Wikipedia. Source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumy_Oblast_Council.

x:Trust_(Doviria).name: Trust (Doviria)
x:Trust_(Doviria).summary: Regional party that came first in the Poltava Oblast Council in 2020. No English Wikipedia article; source: Poltava Oblast Council article, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poltava_Oblast_Council.

Yulia_Tymoshenko_Bloc.name: Yulia Tymoshenko Bloc
Yulia_Tymoshenko_Bloc.summary: Electoral alliance led by Batkivshchyna that came first in most central Ukrainian oblast councils in the 2006 local elections.

UDAR.name: UDAR (Ukrainian Democratic Alliance for Reform)
UDAR.summary: Party led by Vitali Klitschko that won seats in Kyiv and Chernihiv oblast councils in 2010.

Reforms_and_Order_Party.name: Reforms and Order Party
Reforms_and_Order_Party.summary: Liberal party that won two seats in the Chernihiv Oblast Council in 2010.

European_Party_of_Ukraine.name: European Party of Ukraine
European_Party_of_Ukraine.summary: Party of Mykola Katerynchuk that won a seat in the Kyiv Oblast Council in 2010.

Peasant_Party_of_Ukraine.name: Peasant Party of Ukraine
Peasant_Party_of_Ukraine.summary: Agrarian party with a seat in the Poltava Oblast Council after 2010.

Ukrainian_Republican_Party_Sobor.name: Ukrainian Republican Party "Sobor"
Ukrainian_Republican_Party_Sobor.summary: National-democratic party with a seat in the Vinnytsia Oblast Council after 2010.

x:Justice_(Ukraine).name: Justice (Spravedlyvist)
x:Justice_(Ukraine).summary: Small Ukrainian party that won oblast council seats in Kyiv and Kirovohrad oblasts in 2010. No dedicated English Wikipedia article; source: uk.wikipedia oblast council election pages.

x:Third_Force_(Ukraine).name: Third Force
x:Third_Force_(Ukraine).summary: Small party that won one seat in the Kyiv Oblast Council in 2010. No English Wikipedia article; source: uk.wikipedia election page.

x:Conscience_of_Ukraine.name: Conscience of Ukraine
x:Conscience_of_Ukraine.summary: Party that won nine seats in the Poltava Oblast Council in 2010. No English Wikipedia article; source: uk.wikipedia election page.

x:Party_of_Free_Democrats.name: Party of Free Democrats
x:Party_of_Free_Democrats.summary: Small party that won a constituency seat in the Cherkasy Oblast Council in 2010. No English Wikipedia article; source: uk.wikipedia election page.

x:For_Ukraine!.name: For Ukraine!
x:For_Ukraine!.summary: Party that won two seats in the Sumy Oblast Council in 2010. No English Wikipedia article checked; source: uk.wikipedia election page.

x:Ukrainian_Platform.name: Ukrainian Platform
x:Ukrainian_Platform.summary: Small party that won a seat in the Zhytomyr Oblast Council in 2010. No English Wikipedia article; source: uk.wikipedia election page.

x:All-Ukrainian_Chornobyl_People's_Party.name: All-Ukrainian Chornobyl People's Party
x:All-Ukrainian_Chornobyl_People's_Party.summary: Small party that won five seats in the Zhytomyr Oblast Council in 2010. No English Wikipedia article; source: uk.wikipedia election page.

x:All-Ukrainian_Party_of_Spirituality_an.name: All-Ukrainian Party of Spirituality and Patriotism
x:All-Ukrainian_Party_of_Spirituality_an.summary: Small party that won a seat in the Zhytomyr Oblast Council in 2010. No English Wikipedia article; source: uk.wikipedia election page.

x:Civil_Active_of_Kyiv.name: Civil Active of Kyiv
x:Civil_Active_of_Kyiv.summary: Kyiv electoral bloc that won seats in the city council in 2006 and 2008. No English Wikipedia article; source: uk.wikipedia election pages.

x:Vitali_Klitschko_Bloc.name: Vitali Klitschko Bloc
x:Vitali_Klitschko_Bloc.summary: Kyiv electoral bloc led by Vitali Klitschko that came third in the 2008 city council election. No English Wikipedia article; source: uk.wikipedia election page.

x:Mykola_Katerynchuk_Bloc.name: Mykola Katerynchuk Bloc
x:Mykola_Katerynchuk_Bloc.summary: Kyiv electoral bloc of the European Party of Ukraine that cleared the threshold in the 2008 city council election. No English Wikipedia article; source: uk.wikipedia election page.

PORA.name: PORA
PORA.summary: Youth civic campaign of the Orange Revolution that became a party in 2005 and won seats in the Lviv and Chernivtsi councils in 2006.

Lytvyn_Bloc.name: Lytvyn Bloc
Lytvyn_Bloc.summary: Electoral alliance led by parliamentary speaker Volodymyr Lytvyn's People's Party, which ran in the 2006 and 2007 elections.

Ukrainian_People's_Bloc.name: Ukrainian People's Bloc of Kostenko and Plyushch
Ukrainian_People's_Bloc.summary: Electoral alliance of the Ukrainian People's Party and Ivan Plyushch for the 2006 elections, which won seats in most western oblast councils.

Front_for_Change_(Ukraine).name: Front for Change
Front_for_Change_(Ukraine).summary: Arseniy Yatsenyuk's party, which won a few council seats in 2010 and merged into Batkivshchyna in 2013.

Strong_Ukraine.name: Strong Ukraine
Strong_Ukraine.summary: Party of Serhiy Tihipko (formerly the Labour Party of Ukraine) that won seats in eastern councils in 2010 and merged into the Party of Regions in 2012; revived briefly in 2014.

Ukrainian_People's_Party.name: Ukrainian People's Party
Ukrainian_People's_Party.summary: Rukh splinter party founded in 1999 by Hennadiy Udovenko and later led by Yuriy Kostenko, with its base in Galicia and Volhynia.

New_Politics_(Ukraine).name: New Politics
New_Politics_(Ukraine).summary: Party led by former deputy prime minister Volodymyr Semynozhenko, which won six seats in the Zaporizhzhia Oblast Council in 2015.

People's_Opposition_Bloc_of_Natalia_Vitr.name: People's Opposition Bloc of Natalia Vitrenko
People's_Opposition_Bloc_of_Natalia_Vitr.summary: Electoral alliance led by Vitrenko's Progressive Socialist Party, which won seats in several eastern and southern oblast councils in 2006.

Party_of_Industrialists_and_Entrepreneur.name: Party of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs of Ukraine
Party_of_Industrialists_and_Entrepreneur.summary: Business-oriented party founded by Anatoliy Kinakh in 2000; it won single-member seats in some councils in 2010.

1st_Heavy_Mechanized_Brigade.name: 1st Tank Brigade (1st Heavy Mechanized Brigade)
1st_Heavy_Mechanized_Brigade.summary: Armoured brigade based at Honcharivske, Chernihiv Oblast, which fought in the Donbas from 2014 and defended Chernihiv during the 2022 siege.

27th_Artillery_Brigade_(Ukraine).name: 27th Artillery Brigade
27th_Artillery_Brigade_(Ukraine).summary: Rocket artillery brigade based in Sumy, which took part in the defence of Sumy in 2022.

30th_Mechanized_Brigade_(Ukraine).name: 30th Mechanized Brigade
30th_Mechanized_Brigade_(Ukraine).summary: Brigade based in Zviahel (Novohrad-Volynskyi), Zhytomyr Oblast, which fought at Debaltseve in 2015 and in the Donbas after 2022.

43rd_Rocket_Army.name: 43rd Rocket Army
43rd_Rocket_Army.summary: Soviet ICBM army headquartered in Vinnytsia, whose missiles in Ukraine were dismantled after the 1994 Budapest Memorandum.

58th_Motorized_Brigade.name: 58th Motorized Brigade
58th_Motorized_Brigade.summary: Brigade formed in 2015 and based in Konotop, Sumy Oblast, which helped defend Sumy Oblast in 2022 and later fought in the Donbas.

59th_Assault_Brigade.name: 59th Brigade
59th_Assault_Brigade.summary: Brigade formed in 2015 and based at Haisyn, Vinnytsia Oblast, which has fought in the south and in the Donbas.

72nd_Mechanized_Brigade.name: 72nd Mechanized Brigade 'Black Zaporozhians'
72nd_Mechanized_Brigade.summary: Brigade based in Bila Tserkva (Kyiv Oblast) that fought in the Donbas from 2014, defended the western approaches to Kyiv in 2022 and later fought at Vuhledar.

831st_Tactical_Aviation_Brigade.name: 831st Tactical Aviation Brigade
831st_Tactical_Aviation_Brigade.summary: Su-27 fighter brigade based at Myrhorod, Poltava Oblast.

95th_Air_Assault_Brigade.name: 95th Air Assault Brigade
95th_Air_Assault_Brigade.summary: Elite brigade based in Zhytomyr, known for its 2014 raid through the Donbas and for fighting in Kharkiv, Donbas and Kursk operations after 2022.

Aidar_Battalion.name: Aidar Battalion
Aidar_Battalion.type: Volunteer territorial defence battalion, later army assault battalion
Aidar_Battalion.summary: Volunteer battalion formed in May 2014 largely from Euromaidan self-defence members recruited in Kyiv, which fought in Luhansk Oblast.

Aleksey_Fyodorov.name: Fyodorov's Chernihiv partisan formation
Aleksey_Fyodorov.summary: Partisan force led by Chernihiv underground party secretary Oleksii Fedorov, one of the largest in Ukraine, operating in Chernihiv and later Volhynia.

Armed_Forces_of_South_Russia.name: Armed Forces of South Russia
Armed_Forces_of_South_Russia.summary: Denikin's combined White command in 1919-1920, which held left-bank and central Ukraine in autumn 1919.

Armed_Forces_of_Ukraine.name: Armed Forces of Ukraine
Armed_Forces_of_Ukraine.summary: Formed in 1991-1992 largely from Soviet units in Ukraine, including the Kiev Military District.

Austro-Hungarian_Army.name: Austro-Hungarian Army
Austro-Hungarian_Army.summary: Occupied the south-western Ukrainian governorates, including Podolia and parts of Kherson, in 1918.

Azov_Brigade.name: Azov Brigade
Azov_Brigade.type: Volunteer battalion, later a National Guard brigade
Azov_Brigade.summary: Formed in May 2014 by nationalist volunteers, many recruited in Kyiv, as a volunteer battalion; integrated into the National Guard and known for the defence of Mariupol in 2022.

Cheka.name: Cheka
Cheka.summary: Soviet secret police (in Ukraine the VUChK) responsible for the Red Terror, hostage-taking and executions in 1918-1922.

Danylo_Terpylo.name: Otaman Zelenyi's insurgents
Danylo_Terpylo.summary: Peasant army of Danylo Terpylo ('Otaman Zelenyi') from Trypillia, which fought the Hetman, the Bolsheviks and the Whites in the Kyiv region in 1918-1919.

Einsatzkommando.name: Einsatzgruppen / Einsatzkommandos
Einsatzkommando.summary: SS and police units that murdered Jews, Roma and others behind the front; Sonderkommando 4a of Einsatzgruppe C carried out the Babi Yar massacre in Kyiv.

Free_Cossacks.name: Free Cossacks
Free_Cossacks.summary: Peasant self-defence militia that began in Zvenyhorodka county (today Cherkasy Oblast) in spring 1917; its October 1917 congress in Chyhyryn elected Pavlo Skoropadsky as otaman, and it fought for the Central Rada in 1917-1918.

Freedom_of_Russia_Legion.name: Freedom of Russia Legion
Freedom_of_Russia_Legion.summary: Unit of Russian citizens fighting for Ukraine, which joined cross-border raids into Russia, including into Kursk and Belgorod oblasts in 2024.

Georgian_Legion.name: Georgian Legion
Georgian_Legion.summary: Unit of mostly Georgian volunteers formed in 2014, which fought in the Donbas and in the defence of Kyiv Oblast in 2022.

Imperial_German_Army.name: Imperial German Army
Imperial_German_Army.summary: Occupied Ukraine from March to December 1918 under the Brest-Litovsk treaty, first supporting the Central Rada and then installing the Hetmanate of Pavlo Skoropadsky.

International_Legion_(Ukraine).name: International Legion
International_Legion_(Ukraine).summary: Unit of foreign volunteers created in late February 2022 after an appeal by President Zelensky; its first members fought in Kyiv Oblast.

Kholodny_Yar_Republic.name: Kholodny Yar Republic
Kholodny_Yar_Republic.summary: Insurgent territory in the Kholodnyi Yar forest near Chyhyryn that resisted Soviet rule from 1919 until 1922.

Kiev_Military_District.name: Kiev Military District
Kiev_Military_District.summary: Soviet military district headquartered in Kyiv that covered central and northern Ukraine; its forces passed to Ukraine in 1991-1992.

Kyiv_Regiment_(Ukraine).name: Kyiv Regiment
Kyiv_Regiment_(Ukraine).summary: Police special-purpose unit based in Kyiv, which grew out of the 2014 Kyiv police volunteer battalions and fought in Kyiv Oblast and the Donbas after 2022.

Kyiv-1_Police_Battalion.name: Kyiv-1 Battalion
Kyiv-1_Police_Battalion.summary: Volunteer special police battalion formed in Kyiv in 2014 that served in the Donbas war.

Kyiv-2_Company_(Ukraine).name: Kyiv-2
Kyiv-2_Company_(Ukraine).summary: Volunteer special police unit raised in Kyiv in 2014 for service in the Donbas.

Ministry_of_Internal_Affairs_(Soviet_Uni.name: MVD
Ministry_of_Internal_Affairs_(Soviet_Uni.summary: Soviet interior ministry, successor to the NKVD from 1946, whose troops fought the last UPA groups in the late 1940s and early 1950s.

Mykola_Shchors.name: Shchors's Red units (Bohunskyi Regiment, 1st Ukrainian Soviet Division)
Mykola_Shchors.summary: Units raised and commanded by Mykola Shchors from 1918, which fought the UNR in northern and Right-bank Ukraine in 1919 until Shchors was killed that August.

NKVD.name: NKVD
NKVD.summary: Soviet security ministry that carried out the Great Terror of 1937-1938, deportations and, after the war, counter-insurgency against the UPA.

Nykyfor_Hryhoriv.name: Hryhoriv's insurgent army
Nykyfor_Hryhoriv.side: Changing (UNR, then Red Army, then independent)
Nykyfor_Hryhoriv.summary: Forces of otaman Nykyfor Hryhoriv, based around Oleksandriia and Yelisavetgrad, which switched from the Directorate to the Bolsheviks and then rose against them in May 1919, with mass anti-Jewish pogroms.

Organisation_of_Ukrainian_Nationalists.name: Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists
Organisation_of_Ukrainian_Nationalists.summary: Founded in 1929; in 1941 its Melnyk (OUN-M) and Bandera (OUN-B) wings sent 'expeditionary groups' into central Ukraine, where many members were arrested and shot by the Germans in 1942.

Polish_Land_Forces.name: Polish Army
Polish_Land_Forces.summary: In alliance with the UNR, the Polish army advanced through Right-bank Ukraine and took Kyiv in May 1920 before being pushed back by the Red Army.

Poltava_Rifle_Battalion_(Ukraine).name: Poltava Battalion
Poltava_Rifle_Battalion_(Ukraine).summary: Police special-purpose battalion formed in Poltava Oblast in 2014 that served in the Donbas.

Red_Army.name: Red Army
Red_Army.summary: The armed forces of Soviet Russia and later the USSR, which conquered Ukraine in 1919-1920 and fought Germany in 1941-1945.

Red_Guards_(Russia).name: Red Guards
Red_Guards_(Russia).summary: Armed Bolshevik workers' detachments of 1917-1918; in Ukraine they took part in the Kyiv Arsenal uprising and in Muravyov's capture of Kyiv in February 1918.

Revolutionary_Insurgent_Army_of_Ukraine.name: Revolutionary Insurgent Army of Ukraine (Makhnovshchina)
Revolutionary_Insurgent_Army_of_Ukraine.summary: Nestor Makhno's anarchist peasant army based in Huliaipole, which fought Whites, nationalists and Bolsheviks in 1918-1921 and defeated Denikin's forces at Peregonovka near Uman in September 1919.

Russian_Airborne_Forces.name: Russian Airborne Forces (VDV)
Russian_Airborne_Forces.summary: Russian airborne branch whose units landed at Hostomel and occupied Bucha, Irpin and Borodianka in February-March 2022.

Russian_Armed_Forces.name: Russian Armed Forces
Russian_Armed_Forces.summary: Russia's military, which launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022, including the northern offensive on Kyiv, Chernihiv and Sumy, and has since conducted missile and drone strikes across Ukraine.

Russian_Ground_Forces.name: Russian Ground Forces
Russian_Ground_Forces.summary: Russian land army, whose combined-arms and tank armies advanced on Kyiv, Chernihiv and Sumy in 2022 and launched cross-border offensives into Sumy Oblast from 2024-2025.

Russian_Volunteer_Corps.name: Russian Volunteer Corps
Russian_Volunteer_Corps.summary: Unit of Russian nationalist volunteers fighting for Ukraine, known for cross-border raids from northern Ukraine into Russia's Bryansk, Belgorod and Kursk regions.

Sich_Battalion.name: Sich Battalion
Sich_Battalion.summary: Kyiv-based police battalion formed in 2014 from Svoboda-affiliated volunteers, which served in the Donbas war.

Sich_Riflemen.name: Sich Riflemen
Sich_Riflemen.summary: Unit formed in Kyiv in late 1917 from Galician and Bukovinian former Austro-Hungarian prisoners of war under Yevhen Konovalets; it defended the Central Rada and spearheaded the Directorate's 1918 uprising against the Hetman.

Soviet_Army.name: Soviet Army
Soviet_Army.summary: Name of the Soviet ground forces from 1946 to 1991; central Ukraine hosted many of its units under the Kiev Military District.

Soviet_partisans.name: Soviet partisans
Soviet_partisans.summary: Red Army-directed guerrillas behind German lines; the largest Ukrainian formations were based in the northern forests of Sumy, Chernihiv and Zhytomyr oblasts.

Special_Operations_Center_\"East\"_(Ukra.name: 3rd Special Purpose Regiment (Special Operations Center 'East')
Special_Operations_Center_\"East\"_(Ukra.summary: Special forces unit based in Kropyvnytskyi, which fought at Donetsk airport in 2014-2015 and in many operations since 2022.

State_Political_Directorate.name: GPU / OGPU
State_Political_Directorate.summary: Successor of the Cheka from 1922, which suppressed peasant resistance and enforced collectivization and the grain requisitions behind the Holodomor.

Sydir_Kovpak.name: Kovpak's Putyvl partisan unit
Sydir_Kovpak.summary: Partisan formation of Sydir Kovpak, founded in the Spadshchansky forest near Putyvl (Sumy Oblast) in 1941, which raided across Ukraine as far as the Carpathians in 1943.

Territorial_Defence_Forces_(Ukraine).name: Territorial Defence Forces
Territorial_Defence_Forces_(Ukraine).type: Reserve component of the armed forces
Territorial_Defence_Forces_(Ukraine).summary: Separate branch created in January 2022 with a brigade in every oblast and in Kyiv city; many volunteers joined at the start of the full-scale invasion.

Transnistria_Governorate.name: Romanian occupation forces (Transnistria Governorate)
Transnistria_Governorate.summary: Romanian-administered zone between the Dniester and Southern Buh in 1941-1944, which included southern Vinnytsia Oblast and saw the deportation and death of large numbers of Jews.

Ukrainian_Auxiliary_Police.name: Ukrainian Auxiliary Police
Ukrainian_Auxiliary_Police.summary: Local police set up by the German authorities in 1941, used for guard duty and in many places for roundups and killings of Jews.

Ukrainian_Galician_Army.name: Ukrainian Galician Army
Ukrainian_Galician_Army.summary: Army of the West Ukrainian People's Republic which crossed into Podolia in July 1919 and joined the UNR in the advance on Kyiv.

Ukrainian_Insurgent_Army.name: Ukrainian Insurgent Army

Ukrainian_People's_Army.name: Army of the Ukrainian People's Republic

Ukrainian_People's_Revolutionary_Army.name: Ukrainian People's Revolutionary Army (Polissian Sich)
Ukrainian_People's_Revolutionary_Army.summary: Force of Taras Bulba-Borovets formed in 1941 around Olevsk in Polesia, which fought Soviet remnants and later the Germans before being absorbed or destroyed by the OUN-B's UPA in 1943.

Ukrainian_territorial_defence_battalions.name: Territorial defence battalions (2014)

Volunteer_Army.name: Volunteer Army

Imperial_Russian_Army.name: Imperial Russian Army

Polish_insurgents_of_1863.name: Polish insurgents of the January Uprising

Chyhyryn_Secret_Militia.name: Chyhyryn Secret Militia

Berkut_(special_police_force).name: Berkut

politics.note: Kyiv was governed by imperial appointees under the Russian autocracy; after 1906 it sent deputies to the State Duma. It was home to the Old Hromada and, from 1908, the Society of Ukrainian Progressives, and the Ems Ukaz of 1876 banned most Ukrainian printing.

The imperial Kiev Military District was created in 1862 and commanded from the city.

politics.note: Kyiv was the seat of the Central Rada (from March 1917), the Ukrainian People's Republic, the German-backed Hetmanate of Pavlo Skoropadsky (April-December 1918) and the Directorate (December 1918-February 1919). The Rada's governments were led by the Ukrainian Social Democrats and Ukrainian SRs; in the November 1917 Constituent Assembly vote, Ukrainian parties won only about 26% in the largely Russian- and Jewish-speaking city, against 77% in the surrounding Kiev Governorate.

armedGroups.role: Formed in Kyiv in November 1917 and helped crush the Bolshevik Arsenal uprising in January 1918.

Entered Kyiv in March 1918, restored the Rada and in April backed the coup that installed the Hetmanate.
Directorate forces took Kyiv from the Hetman in December 1918 and lost it to the Red Army in February 1919.

politics.note: Control of Kyiv changed hands repeatedly: Soviet rule from February 1919, the UNR and Galician army and Denikin's Whites at the end of August 1919, Soviet rule again from December 1919, the Polish-UNR occupation in May-June 1920, and finally Soviet rule, with Kharkiv as the Soviet Ukrainian capital.

Occupied Kyiv with UNR allies from 7 May to June 1920 during the Kiev offensive.
The Kyiv Cheka carried out mass executions during the Red Terror of 1919.

politics.note: One-party Soviet rule under the Communist Party (Bolsheviks) of Ukraine; Kyiv was a provincial city (the capital was Kharkiv) but a centre of Ukrainization, the Ukrainian Academy of Sciences and the Ukrainian Autocephalous Orthodox Church.

An OUN-M-dominated Ukrainian National Council and city administration were tolerated briefly and then crushed in early 1942. The Red Army retook the city on 6 November 1943.

OUN-M activists ran the city administration in late 1941 until the Gestapo arrested and shot many of them at Babi Yar in 1942.
Liberated Kyiv on 6 November 1943 after crossing the Dnieper.

The 1990 city council, elected in the first semi-free elections, had a strong democratic opposition (seat figures not sourced).

Leonid Chernovetskyi won the mayoralty in 2006 and 2008 with his own bloc; after he left in 2012, Oleksandr Popov of the Party of Regions headed the city administration until January 2014. Detailed council results for 2006 and 2008 could not be sourced.
